confusions: The recipe 'code_review_basics' lists 5 templates and one extra rule, but the skill also says one policy per template: that produces 6 files for one ask. I followed it, but it is not obvious whether a team wants six policies or one combined policy.

LOG-010's template covers only api.request; the limits text says to add stream.from_request, ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.*.direct_query to cover every outbound call, but the template rule itself does not include them. I did not change the template's rule, so coverage is narrower than the ask implies.

CHG-001 template uses object.test_coverage on query only; the recipe's extra rule for functions is not in any template, so I wrote it into REVIEW-001 myself; I was guessing the param shape from the check description.

The parse summary output (default format) omits the severity line for medium-severity policies (LOG-010, PERF-001), while the -o json output keeps it. This looks like a display quirk, and I could not tell from the skill whether medium is the default and is therefore dropped.

Template 'Fill' says _nothing_ for most template rules, but the actual template rules include more params than the table shows (e.g. CONV-040 has max_statements and max_nesting, not a fill). Fine, but the skill could say the template values are the rule values.

The skill says a policy file may carry tags only when the workspace has them or they are proposed; the template frameworks field maps to tags. I put soc2 on CHG-001 without knowing whether the workspace has a soc2 tag. It is an unverified tag, and the skill's rule is unclear on whether framework tags are created or just referenced.
wished_for: A ready-made 'code review basics' example file set under policies/ so the six-file pattern is copy-able
A way to see, from the catalogue, which external statements a template rule covers, not only its limits text
Guidance on whether a policy can cover a set of templates in one file (the recipe's 'one policy per template' vs. one combined policy)
A catalogue example for object.test_coverage on functions, and for what counts as a test calling a function
why_confidence: The files parse with no rule warnings, and five templates plus one extra rule cover error handling on HTTP calls, untested endpoints/functions, long stacks, leftover code, and unbounded reads. Confidence is only medium because: (1) the ask is about stopping prod breakage, which no check reads; (2) LOG-010 covers api.request only, and the workspace has other outbound calls; (3) 'tested' is checked for existence, not quality; (4) I did not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden in this run), so the findings each rule would produce on the workspace are predictions, not observations. Predictions: PERF-001 will report invoices_GET because per_page comes from input; CHG-001 will likely report most endpoints because only two smoke tests exist; CONV-040 may report acme_sync_shipping_rates, which the file comment says has grown over time.
